scope: Corollary 6.4 (Effect of deletion on constant spaces) of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-the-Kadison-Kaplansky-Projection-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df6227b615985805), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Π be the orthogonal projection that retains the vertices of Y in the counting Hilbert space of the full tower, with any additional Hilbert- space tensor factor. Let C be the subspace of vectors that are constant on each separate Ai and Bi in the vertex coordinate. Then ∥(1 − Π)|C∥ ≤ √ εℓ. In particular the same bound holds on every subspace of C, uniformly in the additional tensor factor.
